login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified in the authorization/token request, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: JWT-specific tests must request a resource or organization context; otherwise opaque-token behavior is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission or role changes do not modify existing JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect updated scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag old-token continued access before expiry as stale-cache vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep previously granted scopes until they expire, even after permissions are reduced.
oidc_jwt.note: Only newly issued tokens reflect permission reductions immediately.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, refresh does not enlarge scopes beyond the original authorization request set.
oidc_jwt.note: A missing newly granted scope after refresh is expected unless a new authorization flow is performed.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange requests fail unless the application explicitly enables token exchange.
oidc_jwt.note: A rejection in this state is expected and not evidence of proper audience/scope enforcement.

oidc_jwt.description: User organization tokens are not returned directly from the authorization code flow; a refresh-token step is required to obtain them.
oidc_jwt.note: Treat absence of direct organization token in code flow as by design, not a token issuance failure.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, refresh cannot enlarge scopes beyond those requested in the original OAuth authorization flow.
oidc_jwt.note: A new authorization flow is required for newly granted scopes outside the original request set.

oidc_jwt.description: If organization_id is omitted from the token request, Logto evaluates only global roles and permissions.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing organization context is not an org-isolation bypass; it selects the global authorization model.

oidc_jwt.description: MFA validation is bypassed for users signing in via enterprise SSO because the upstream IdP is treated as trusted.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag absence of local MFA challenge after enterprise SSO as a broker-side MFA bypass bug.

oidc_jwt.description: If a default API resource is configured, omitting the resource parameter causes Logto to use that default API resource as the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: A non-empty aud claim in this case is expected and not evidence that audience checks were bypassed.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct sign-in fails because the connector is missing or disabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: Fallback is expected behavior, not flow confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to an existing Logto user when the working email matches an existing account.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-source identity merge on matching email is by design for enterprise SSO and should not be flagged as unintended collision.

oidc_jwt.description: End-session clears the centralized Logto session, but if offline_access was granted the app grant may remain valid until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Refresh capability after browser logout can be expected unless explicit revocation is performed.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: JWT-specific validation or claim-inspection tests must not treat opaque-token issuance as a bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Logto issues JWT access tokens for API resources only when a resource or organization context is requested. If no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT. For oidc_jwt tests, the fuzzer MUST request a resource parameter (or organization token context) when obtaining the session token; otherwise JWT-based invariants are untestable and failures are false positives.

The resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI). Logto does not support wildcard or prefix matching for resource indicators. For audience-binding tests, use exact absolute URI values; do not fuzz with partial prefixes unless the test expects rejection.

Scope names must exactly match the permission names defined for the API resource. There is no wildcard, prefix, or shorthand matching. For I5 multi-permission tests, the fuzzer MUST request the exact scope strings; values like 'read' will not match 'read:elections'.

For global API resources, permission enlargement is not reflected by refresh alone if the newly desired scopes were not part of the original authorization request. A new OAuth authorization flow is required to obtain newly granted scopes outside the original request set. For I3 config-change tests, do not expect refresh_token reuse to pick up broadened scope requests automatically.

Existing JWTs are immutable. When roles or permissions are reduced, only newly issued tokens reflect the reduced scopes; existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiration. For I3 coherence tests after policy tightening, the fuzzer MUST obtain a new token after the change and MUST NOT treat continued acceptance of an old unexpired JWT as stale-policy vulnerability by itself.

Organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. For organization-scoped I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST include organization_id in the token request; otherwise acceptance under global roles is by design, not a cross-org escalation bug.

Organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. Logto requires refresh_token flow or client_credentials flow with organization parameters to obtain organization tokens. For organization-context oidc_jwt tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token (or use client credentials) and then call /oidc/token with organization_id.

Organization tokens are always JWTs, while opaque tokens cannot be used as organization tokens. For tests that need organization_id and organization-scoped permissions in JWT claims, the fuzzer MUST use refresh_token or client_credentials with organization parameters, not opaque-token userinfo flows.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running token_exchange tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled in application settings; otherwise 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' is expected behavior, not a security rejection oracle.

PAT token exchange uses /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and subject_token_type=urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. The fuzzer MUST use that exact subject_token_type for PAT-based exchange tests; other token-type values are not equivalent.

The token endpoint and revocation/introspection endpoints use application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies. If the fuzzer sends JSON, the request is malformed. This especially affects exchange_code_for_token, token_exchange, revoke_session, and introspect_token.

OIDC user authentication in Logto is redirect-based; direct credential submission from the client app is not supported, and ROPC is deprecated/not available. For oidc_jwt login tests, the fuzzer MUST use the authorization endpoint flow rather than attempting login_with_password-style direct token acquisition.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWT validation in protected APIs, include a control token request that should succeed under the same resource/scope setup. Without a valid control, a 401 on the attack token may reflect wrong audience/resource/scope setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Logto validation guidance explicitly verifies issuer and expiration, but many code examples disable automatic audience verification and require manual audience checks based on permission model. For I1/I5 audience tests, the fuzzer MUST ensure the relying API under test actually checks aud against the requested resource indicator; otherwise acceptance of wrong-audience tokens may be an application misconfiguration, not a Logto token issuance flaw.

When testing cross-provider or wrong-audience acceptance, remember that Logto's JWTs may contain aud as either a string or an array depending on library/framework handling. The oracle MUST normalize aud to a list before comparison to avoid false positives from type differences.

For sign-out and revocation tests, clearing local client state is not equivalent to revoking the centralized Logto session or grant. If offline_access was granted, end-session does not revoke the grant by default and refresh-token chains may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. The fuzzer MUST distinguish local logout, end-session, and token revocation when asserting I2 freshness or session invalidation.

Current Logto SDK signOut behavior is effectively global sign-out via /session/end and /session/end/confirm with logout=true. For I3 multi-app/session tests, a sign-out in one app may clear the centralized Logto session for the current browser by design; do not interpret cross-app logout in the same browser as session confusion.

If offline_access is granted, end-session does not revoke the app grant by default, and the default grant TTL is 180 days. For I2 revocation/freshness tests, the fuzzer MUST use explicit token revocation or grant-aware expectations; continued refresh capability after browser logout can be by design.

Direct sign-in parameters are only shortcuts on the authorization request and still route through /oidc/auth. If direct_sign_in target is missing or disabled, fallback to the standard sign-in page is by design. The fuzzer MUST not treat fallback as flow confusion or auth bypass.

For OIDC request customization tests, ui_locales, first_screen, identifier, login_hint, and direct_sign_in are interaction-shaping parameters only. They do not alter token audience or permission grants. The fuzzer MUST not use differences in UI routing as authorization or principal-binding oracles.

When validating JWTs against Logto JWKS, the issuer is fixed to https://<tenant>/oidc and JWKS URI is fixed to https://<tenant>/oidc/jwks. Logto does not support customizing issuer or JWKS URI. For trust-anchor substitution tests, the fuzzer must target issuer/JWKS mismatch at the relying party configuration layer, not assume tenant-side alternate issuer settings exist.

For token exchange impersonation tests using actor_token, the resulting token may include an act claim identifying the actor. Presence of act is by design when actor_token is supplied. The oracle MUST compare sub for impersonated principal and treat act.sub as actor metadata, not as a principal-collision signal.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, the fuzzer MUST include a control token request that succeeds under the same client/resource setup. A failed attack token request alone is ambiguous because Logto also rejects misconfigured client_id, client_secret, resource, scope, or organization_id combinations.

The resource parameter is exact-match only. Logto requires the requested resource to exactly match the registered API identifier URI; wildcards or prefixes are not supported. For I5 and cross-audience tests, use concrete distinct resource URIs. For multi-identity scenarios, do NOT set resource to '*' expecting a wildcard.

Scope names are exact-match only. Requested scopes must exactly match permission names defined in Logto; prefixes or shortened names do not act as wildcards. For I5 tests, use full permission strings and do NOT use '*' or partial names to simulate broad matching.

When testing JWT-vs-opaque behavior, the fuzzer MUST request a resource if it needs a JWT access token. If no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. This is by design and would invalidate JWT-claim-based or signature-based test assumptions.

If a default API resource is configured, omitting resource does not mean 'no audience restriction'; Logto will use the default API resource as the audience for tokens. I5 empty_audience tests MUST account for this and should not interpret a JWT with aud set by default-resource behavior as audience validation bypass.

For organization-scoped token tests, organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. I5 organization-bound authorization tests MUST include organization_id on the token request.

Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. To obtain an organization token after interactive login, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Do not treat missing organization claims on the initial code exchange as a vulnerability.

For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set; a new authorization flow is required for newly granted scopes outside the original request. I3 permission-change tests MUST distinguish stale-token behavior from the documented scope-subset rule.

An access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. Even after role changes, newly issued tokens are limited to a subset of the originally requested scopes. I5 escalation tests MUST request the candidate scopes in the original flow if they expect them to ever appear later.

Permission changes are reflected only in newly issued JWTs; existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. I3 config-change and authorization-tightening tests MUST obtain a fresh token after the change and MUST NOT expect already-issued JWTs to mutate in place.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running RFC 8693 tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected and are not evidence of correct audience or scope enforcement.

For PAT or impersonation token exchange tests, the token endpoint accepts either HTTP Basic client authentication or client_id in the form body depending on client type. The fuzzer MUST use a confidential client with Basic auth when a client secret exists, and a public client with body client_id otherwise, to avoid false negatives unrelated to token-exchange security.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the token endpoint /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and vary the resource parameter as the target audience. Logto documentation models audience selection through resource indicators, not a separate audience field.

For organization token exchange and client-credentials tests, organization permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions. The fuzzer MUST not interpret rejection of mixed-scope requests as over-enforcement bugs; mixed global and organization permission models are unsupported by design.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on Logto-issued tokens, the expected issuer is fixed to https://<tenant>/oidc and is discoverable from /oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration. Since Logto does not allow customizing issuer or JWKS URI, tests should vary the token issuer claim or trust source, not attempt admin-side issuer reconfiguration through OIDC endpoints.

For I2 replay_same_token against ordinary JWT bearer access tokens, replay is expected by design unless additional application-side state is enforced. Logto documentation describes stateless JWT validation and does not document jti replay tracking for bearer access tokens. Do not flag same-token reuse alone as a vulnerability.

For sign-out and revocation tests, revoking a token or ending the Logto session does not necessarily revoke grants that have offline_access. End-session keeps offline_access grants until grant TTL expiry. I2/I3 tests MUST distinguish session logout from refresh-token/grant invalidation.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. The documentation specifies a default nonzero lifetime but does not document 0 as 'immediate expiry' or 'disable'. Never assume 0 disables issuance or means literal zero without separate API confirmation.

Logto issues JWT access tokens only when a specific API resource or organization context is requested. If no resource is specified, the access token is opaque and intended for /oidc/me or introspection. For oidc_jwt tests that require JWT claim validation, the fuzzer MUST request a resource or organization token; otherwise it may receive an opaque token and misclassify failures.

The resource parameter is exact-match only. The requested resource MUST exactly match the registered API identifier URI; wildcards or prefixes are not supported. For I5 audience tests, use the exact registered URI for control cases and a different exact URI for mismatch cases.

Scope names are exact-match only. Requested scopes must exactly match permission names defined for the API resource; shortened prefixes or wildcard-like values do not match. For multi-permission tests, request the full explicit scope names.

For global API resources, if the original authorization flow did not request a scope, later refreshes cannot enlarge the token beyond the originally requested scope set. A valid I5 scope-escalation test MUST compare against the original requested scopes and use a fresh authorization flow when testing newly requested scopes, not just refresh.

For organization tokens, request organization context explicitly. Without organization_id, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced. Any I5 organization-scope or tenant-isolation test MUST include organization_id in the token request.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running any RFC 8693 token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected setup errors rather than security behavior.

The /oidc/token endpoint requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded bodies for authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, and token_exchange grants; JSON bodies are not valid for these documented OIDC endpoints.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, include a control token request that should succeed under the same client/resource configuration. Otherwise a token acquisition failure may be caused by missing resource, missing organization_id, or disabled grant configuration rather than freshness enforcement.

Audience validation is not automatically enforced in the sample API validation logic; the documentation explicitly shows verify_aud/ValidateAudience disabled and says audience must be checked manually based on permission model. When testing I5 audience binding in relying-party sample apps, the oracle MUST verify that the application under test actually checks aud/resource rather than assuming the framework does it by default.

Issuer validation is expected and documented as mandatory for Logto-issued JWT validation. For I1 trust-anchor or forged-issuer tests, the control configuration MUST use the tenant issuer from discovery or https://<tenant>/oidc exactly; mismatched issuer should be rejected.

Signing key rotation changes the active JWKS immediately in Cloud, but existing tokens signed by the previous key remain valid until that previous key is removed. For I3 key-rotation coherence tests, do NOT expect old tokens to fail immediately after a single rotation if the previous key is still published in JWKS. A rejection oracle is valid only after the previous key is removed or no longer trusted by the verifier.

Never interpret repeated acceptance of the same self-contained JWT as a replay vulnerability by itself. JWT bearer replay/jti tracking is not documented as enforced for Logto-issued stateless JWT access tokens. replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti are hardening checks, not vulnerabilities, unless the context is one-time subject tokens or other explicitly one-time artifacts.
oidc_jwt.source: developers/custom-token-claims/create-script.mdx (jti field presence only); general Logto JWT issuance docs lack jti replay tracking guarantees

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token exchange using personal access tokens, subject_token_type must be exactly urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. Using other subject_token_type values changes the flow semantics and invalidates PAT-based test setup.

PAT-obtained access tokens are documented to behave identically to refresh-token-obtained access tokens for organization context and permissions. Therefore, differences between PAT exchange and refresh-token exchange should not be treated as expected by-design narrowing; they should be investigated as potential inconsistencies.

Current SDK sign-out behavior is global sign-out at the Logto session layer, but grants with offline_access are not revoked by end-session and may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. For I3/I2 logout tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish 'browser SSO session cleared' from 'refresh-capable grant revoked'. A still-working refresh token after end-session can be by design when offline_access was granted.

Default grant TTL is 180 days, and offline_access grants can survive end-session until grant expiration unless explicitly revoked. Freshness tests that assume logout invalidates all downstream tokens will produce false positives unless they separately revoke the token/grant or avoid offline_access.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
